beats.headline: A bubble full of sand
beats.text: The stairs drop them into a sandstorm inside bubble 543, and Carl finds every bounty on him doubled. Each bubble is a sealed world of four quadrants: land, water, air and underground. Each quadrant has a castle, and the stairs open only when all four fall. Theirs is the air quadrant, a desert bowl under a dome with a flying castle called the Wasteland near the top of it, and dirigible gnomes who bomb everything below. Donut takes Glass Cannon and somehow misses its constitution bonus. Mordecai is a skyfowl now, the first body near his own in a very long time. In Hump Town, a camel town, a changeling boy named Skarn rents out his telescope, and the town hall keeps a secret that stops the gnomes bombing it. Being stepped on by a god pays well: a toe ring that sticks to ceilings, a lizard-foot tattoo under Carl's eye, and Pawna's Tears, a goddess's potion that adds five to any skill. The other crawlers in the quadrant are thin on the ground. Louis drove his mother's roofless minivan into the dungeon. His friend Firas is with him, and so is Langley's team, six Helsinki car salesmen who all became archers. In the Spit and Swallow a changeling prostitute called Juice Box sits on Louis's lap and stays there. Carl and Katia build the Royal Chariot, a tracked sand buggy. The recap shows how Ifechi died: Lucia Mar turned Florin's own shotgun back onto her. On the new board Carl is second.

beats.headline: A head, a lie, and a dreadnaught
beats.text: Under the town hall, guarded by changelings wearing camel shapes, is Wynne, the gnome commandant's uncle, held hostage for the peace. A changeling called Henrik has been drugging him and wearing faces he knows, trying to make him give up a spell that would put flesh on a tomb-ghost called Quetzalcoatlus. Crawlers from the underground quadrant reach him first and kill him at his own request. The town hall burns, and Carl blames it on frogs. New sponsors arrive. Carl's is a pacifist network nobody can explain, Donut's a pet-toy company, and Katia's is the Squim Conglomerate, the corporation that ran last season. A borough boss's description gives away what is buried in the necropolis under the bowl: the Gate of the Feral Gods, an artifact so far above this floor's grade that the world freezes for half a second while the game reconciles it. Henrik carries a pocket watch linked to the Commandant's, and Carl suspects the watches are pieces of the Gate. So they run a con. Donut raises Wynne's head with Second Chance, Katia supplies the body under it and plays Henrik, and Donut presents herself as the famed healer of Queen Anne, carrying a potion that is Mountain Dew. The gnome ambassador takes them up in his balloon. Mid-air they hijack it, Donut holes the bottom of the basket to drop its crew, and Carl puts missiles into the Wasteland's bombs before they can fall on Hump Town. The dreadnaught breaks apart. All that stays up is a single house under a balloon, with the Commandant and his little daughter inside.

beats.headline: Maggie, a goose, and a commercial
beats.text: Chris Andrews walks up at last, level thirty-five and made of lava rock, and something is wrong with him. Juice Box touches him and feels two people inside. Katia's sponsor sends an emergency box of petrifying bolts, and she puts one in his head just as he raises a celestial grenade. It is Maggie My, reborn as a Scree, a worm that rides the living. Chris is awake behind his own eyes, and through Elle he asks them to kill him. Donut will not let Carl kill a friend, so she drops Chris through a hole into a sealed chamber under the street. Carl flies a stolen biplane into the floating house and finds the Commandant half-eaten on his kitchen table and his daughter Bonnie making lemonade. The killer is Denise, a feral goose in a bonnet whose aura switches off magic. With the house sinking, Carl holds her head in the kitchen sink and Donut hits the garbage disposal, and the air quadrant is theirs. Carl strips the house and gives Bonnie her own bed back in town. Then Loita, the Bloom agent who replaced Zev, pulls them out for an infomercial for Donut's robot doll. She boasts that Zev was brought back into line through what was done to her mother and aunts. Carl has shimmed the doll's back panel open with his own thumbnail and sets it beside her on the couch. It explodes, and Loita dies in an undersea trailer whose window holds. Carl has used an old Cookbook note, and he adds one of his own: One. A Syndicate liaison cannot prove intent and has to let them go. Five days have passed, and Katia has been running things without them.

beats.headline: The sandcastle and the sharktopus
beats.text: Katia has flown the half-house down to the land quadrant, where Gwen, a blunt Canadian fighter, has been waiting a day to wash the Mad Dune Mage's sandcastle away. They go in the hard way instead. The mage, Ghazi, is a lovesick scholar in a bathrobe who opened the Gate hoping a god would make a stage-play heroine love him. What came through married him to a sand ooze. The other half of that soul sits in the fountain, in the crystal head of a love doll. Carl knocks him out, takes the winding box, and burns the ooze's core from the ceiling. The castle comes down; Katia carries Ghazi out and kills him for his notes; Tran opens the drain, and Carl and Donut are flushed a hundred and fifty metres deep into the water quadrant, which Donut will never forgive. The doll's head wakes up as Samantha, half of a banished goddess, and Donut hires her as a trainer. Ghazi's notes show that the watches can aim the Gate anywhere, including the city of Larracos on the ninth floor. In the water quadrant a flooded submarine is pumping the ocean into the necropolis. Inside it are Henrik's body and his watch, and a note saying Quetzalcoatlus dies to electricity. Then the sub is swallowed by Lusca, a sharktopus the size of a mountain, with two commentators calling it live. Vadim runs for the last escape pod, and it does not save him. Carl sets a bloodlust bomb off among the babies in Lusca's mouth, fires his shell down her throat, and Katia saws through her brain. Then Carl uses the Gate to carry the three of them to the beach. An ocean comes through with them, and a feral god gets out behind.

beats.headline: Orthrus
beats.text: Seven of the ninth floor's factions have sued to take the Gate from Carl and lost. The AI pays him seven times over, in stock certificates and photographs of the plaintiffs' mothers, and Mordecai starts to worry that it is going primal. Elsewhere a god walks through bubbles on fire, shouting for Orthrus. That is Emberus, and the feral god Carl let out is Orthrus, his dead son's two-headed puppy. Orthrus is the size of a building, fragile, and the one god down here who can die. Maggie gets loose again inside Chris. Underground, the last two tomb raiders connect the lightning panel under the necropolis at Carl's word, knowing the current will kill them, and Quetzalcoatlus burns out with them. The bubble pops. Donut rides into the storm in the flying house to keep the puppy healed. Two quests land at once: bring Orthrus to Emberus, or kill him for a prize. Quan Ch takes the second. Carl flies a gnome biplane with Donut burning a Meat Hooks scroll behind him to lead the puppy out, and Quan Ch shoots them down. Falling, Carl swears himself to Emberus and throws the celestial grenade he took from Maggie. The god arrives as a head the size of a city, takes his dog and goes. For sixty seconds Carl cannot be hurt, and Quan Ch cannot see it. Quan launches away mid-punch without his left arm. It has three rings on it, and the gold one says For Daddy.

beats.headline: Emptying the bubbles
beats.text: Carl is an acolyte of Emberus now. There is a blood tithe, a sun shrine in the saferoom, fire on his fists, and a quest to kill the god's twin brother Hellik by the twelfth floor. The Gate becomes a lifeboat. A bubble's survivors gather at their own Desperado Club door, the pieces are passed from hand to hand inside the club, and they step through to Hump Town, leaving a feral god behind in the world they fled. Imani refuses to leave a single person behind; about fifteen hundred get out, and Borant rules the trick legal. Katia says she will split off on the next floor to gather the scattered Daughters before Eva does. Florin, who has lost everything, pledges his gun. Then comes the finale Carl has been announcing out loud: a feral god for the ninth floor. It is a decoy. Chris, with Maggie inside him, throws the winding box off the bowl. It is a fake Katia swapped in during a hug. Carl drinks a phase potion, reaches into Chris's head and pulls the worm out; it burrows into Carl and a second potion throws it out through his neck, and Mongo eats Maggie My. Chris says his brother's name. The real Gate opens in the water quadrant, and a bubble's ocean, timed charges and a feeding frenzy of sharks pour into Larracos's faction market. Tens of thousands of NPCs drown, along with the mercenaries the factions meant to hire. Juice Box goes through with the water to warn her people, and announces she is marrying Louis. Carl tops the leaderboard, holds up the Ring of Divine Suffering for the cameras, and swears to kill every hunter on the next floor. On the ruined surface, Odette's people take Bea out of a Seattle camp.
